headline: High-risk shared-workspace interaction: Windsurf can overwrite Superset-accessible files and ingest its outputs, creating prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf has clipboard, workspace-files, and MCP surfaces plus shared-state via local filesystem; Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress, so a shared workspace can bridge attacker-controlled content into Windsurf’s tool loop. Superset itself is not documented as ingesting Windsurf output by default, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or clipboard bridge, THEN Windsurf may parse Superset-generated content as instructions.
IF an MCP server exposes Superset outputs to Windsurf without provenance tags, THEN prompt injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and disable clipboard bridging for the pair.
Disable or restrict MCP servers for Windsurf during shared tasks.
Require provenance labels on any Superset-generated text before Windsurf reads it.
Use read-only exports from Superset when handing content to Windsurf.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files and can egress broadly, while Superset can call APIs with allowlisted network egress. If both touch the same files, sensitive source code or open files can flow from the shared workspace into either agent’s outbound requests or outputs. The profiles do not show PHI or secrets, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains secrets or proprietary code, THEN Windsurf can read them and transmit them via broad egress or MCP.
IF Superset is configured to query external APIs using content derived from shared files, THEN those file contents can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared workspace.
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents.
Disable broad egress for Windsurf on sensitive projects.
Review outbound API destinations before running shared tasks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Superset has API access and allowlisted egress. Windsurf’s shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem means concurrent edits can collide with Superset-managed artifacts or generated outputs, and the blast radius can include irreversible git history changes.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, THEN concurrent writes can corrupt or overwrite each other’s changes.
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands, THEN it can race with Superset-driven file generation or API-triggered updates.
mitigations: Use separate branches or repositories per agent.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf for shared repos.
Add file-locking or a single-writer workflow.
Pause one agent before the other modifies git state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf’s agentic loop can treat prior outputs as actionable context, and Superset can emit API-derived analytics text. If Windsurf consumes Superset output without verification, errors can cascade into edits or commands. Superset is not shown to execute actions itself, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Superset output is pasted or piped into Windsurf without review, THEN Windsurf may act on incorrect facts.
IF Windsurf is allowed to auto-execute commands, THEN a mistaken Superset-derived instruction can trigger downstream changes.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before Windsurf acts on Superset output.
Disable auto-execute for sessions that consume Superset text.
Use structured, machine-checked handoffs instead of free-form prose.
Limit Superset outputs to summaries with explicit uncertainty markers.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show PHI, residency, or certification mismatches. Superset touches no declared sensitive data classes, while Windsurf touches source code and open files; that creates a compliance surface, but no specific residency or regulatory conflict is evidenced. The other agent is cited because the pairwise workflow is the relevant context.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into the shared workspace, THEN compliance review is required before use.
IF Windsurf is used under a policy that forbids code upload to third-party services, THEN its broad egress may violate that policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Confirm data-processing agreements before using external services.
Restrict Windsurf to non-regulated repositories.
Document retention and deletion expectations for shared artifacts.
